title: Where does the money go? The price of a chocolate bar

task.situation:
Your school’s student council would like the school shop to sell fairer snacks and is planning a week of events on fair trade. It has asked your class to write a report based on the following chart, which the council has drawn up as a simplified example. All figures are invented, but realistic.
Chart: ‘Where does the money go? How the price of a €2.50 chocolate bar is shared out’
• retailer (shop rent, staff and profit): 38% (€0.95)
• brand (recipe, advertising and profit): 26% (€0.65)
• processing (factory, sugar, milk and packaging): 16% (€0.40)
• taxes: 10% (€0.25)
• cocoa farmers: 6% (€0.15)
• transport and shipping: 4% (€0.10)
task.instruction: Write a report for the student council in which you:
points: outline how the price of the chocolate bar is shared out
explain the effects on cocoa farmers and consumers
recommend what the school community could do, for example in the school shop or at school events

words.short: Divide your report into sections and give them headings. Write around 250 words.
words.long: Divide your report into sections and give them headings. Write around 400 words.

task.de: Report an die Schüler:innenvertretung auf Basis einer erfundenen Beispielgrafik: Wie teilt sich der Preis einer Tafel Schokolade um 2,50 Euro auf? Drei Inhaltspunkte: Anteile beschreiben, Folgen für Kakaobäuer:innen und Konsument:innen erklären, Empfehlungen für die Schulgemeinschaft (Schulbuffet, Veranstaltungen). Abschnitte mit Zwischenüberschriften, formell, keine Kurzformen.

focus.label: passive forms and data phrases
focus.note: Marked: passive verb forms (is shared out, are paid, be displayed, could be set up …) and phrases that present, compare and interpret figures (according to the chart, accounts for, the largest share, followed by, more than six times as much as, a rise of 6 per cent …). Numbers on their own, participles used as adjectives (a simplified example, the planned week) and general linking words are not marked.

gaps.q: What is the school’s week of events called? Give it a name.
gaps.qDe: Wie heißt die Aktionswoche an der Schule? Gebt ihr einen englischen Namen, z. B. „Fair Food Week“.

steps.q: Which subject line do we put in the header?
steps.de: Die Betreffzeile sagt, worum es im Report geht.
steps.own: Factual and specific: what is the report about?
steps.ownDe: Sachlich und genau: Worum geht es im Report?

options.label: Data plus purpose
options.text: Price breakdown of a €2.50 chocolate bar: findings and recommendations
options.why: Factual and complete: it names the data and tells the council that recommendations follow.

options.label: A question turned into a statement
options.text: Where the money for a €2.50 chocolate bar goes
options.why: Short and clear, a little livelier, but still factual.

options.label: Analysis and aim
options.text: Who earns what from a chocolate bar: analysis and recommendations
options.why: Names the main question of the report and both of its parts.

steps.q: How do we open the report?
steps.de: Der erste Abschnitt nennt Zweck, Auftrag und Datenquelle des Reports. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete the introduction: state the purpose and the source of the data.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Einleitung fertigschreiben: Zweck und Datenquelle nennen.

options.label: State the aim
options.text:
### Introduction
{{The aim of this report is to}} examine how the price of a €2.50 chocolate bar [[is shared out]] and how this affects cocoa farmers and consumers. {{It [[is based]] on the council’s chart, which [[breaks down]]}} the price into six shares.
options.why: Purpose and data source first: a classic report opening.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
{{The aim of this report is to}} examine how the price of a €2.50 chocolate bar [[is shared out]] and how this affects cocoa farmers and consumers. {{It [[is based]] on the council’s chart, which [[breaks down]]}} the price into six shares. {{These figures should [[be read]] with care,}} as they [[describe]] a single simplified example. {{Even so, [[they point to]] a pattern}} that is typical of the chocolate trade.

options.label: Refer to the request
options.text:
### Introduction
{{At the request of the student council, this report}} looks at the council’s chart, {{which [[shows]] how}} the price of a €2.50 chocolate bar [[is divided]]. {{It also considers}} the effects on cocoa farmers and consumers and makes recommendations.
options.why: Names who asked for the report, which data it uses and what follows.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
{{At the request of the student council, this report}} looks at the council’s chart, {{which [[shows]] how}} the price of a €2.50 chocolate bar [[is divided]]. {{It also considers}} the effects on cocoa farmers and consumers and makes recommendations. {{One limitation is that the chart does not [[show]]}} how the shares differ between brands, {{or whether}} the price of fairly traded chocolate [[is shared out]] in the same way.

options.label: Start with the figures
options.text:
### Introduction
The retailer receives 38 per cent of the price of a €2.50 chocolate bar, and the brand gets 26 per cent. Processing accounts for 16 per cent, taxes for 10 per cent and transport for 4 per cent, while the cocoa farmers get only 6 per cent, or 15 cents.
options.reject: This jumps straight into the figures. A report first states its purpose, who asked for it and where the data comes from; the figures belong in the next section.
options.rejectDe: Hier geht es sofort mit den Zahlen los. Ein Report nennt zuerst Zweck, Auftrag und Datenquelle; die Zahlen gehören in den nächsten Abschnitt.
options.textLong:
### Introduction
The retailer receives 38 per cent of the price of a €2.50 chocolate bar, and the brand gets 26 per cent. Processing accounts for 16 per cent, taxes for 10 per cent and transport for 4 per cent, while the cocoa farmers get only 6 per cent, or 15 cents. Taxes alone take 25 cents, which is more than the farmers receive for all the cocoa in the bar.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then state the purpose and the source of the data, and explain in your own words why the figures should be read with care.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Zweck und Datenquelle nennen und mit eigenen Worten erklären, warum man die Zahlen vorsichtig lesen muss.

steps.q: Body paragraph 1 (content point 1): how do we outline the shares of the price?
steps.de: Der erste Hauptteil beschreibt die Anteile am Preis aus der Grafik. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then add the missing figures from the chart in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die fehlenden Zahlen aus der Grafik mit eigenen Worten ergänzen.

options.label: From largest to smallest
options.text:
### Analysis of the findings
{{[[According to the chart]], [[the largest share]],}} 38 per cent or 95 cents, goes to the retailer. {{The brand [[accounts for]]}} 26 per cent, [[followed by]] processing (16 per cent) and taxes (10 per cent). {{[[The smallest shares]] go to}} the cocoa farmers (6 per cent or 15 cents) and transport (4 per cent).
options.why: Goes through the chart in order of size, so the reader can follow every figure.
options.textLong:
### Analysis of the findings
{{[[According to the chart]], [[the largest share]],}} 38 per cent or 95 cents, goes to the retailer. {{The brand [[accounts for]]}} 26 per cent, [[followed by]] processing (16 per cent) and taxes (10 per cent). {{[[The smallest shares]] go to}} the cocoa farmers (6 per cent or 15 cents) and transport (4 per cent). {{This [[reveals]] a striking gap:}} the retailer receives [[more than six times as much as]] the cocoa farmers, and {{even the brand earns [[over four times as much as]]}} they do.

options.label: Selling versus growing
options.text:
### Analysis of the findings
{{[[As the chart makes clear,]] [[most of the money]] [[is earned]]}} far from the cocoa farms. {{[[Almost two thirds]] goes to}} the retailer and the brand, while taxes and transport {{[[make up]]}} 14 per cent. {{Production, by contrast, [[accounts for]] [[just over a fifth]]}} (16 per cent for processing, 6 per cent for the farmers).
options.why: Groups the six shares into blocks, which already shows the main finding.
options.textLong:
### Analysis of the findings
{{[[As the chart makes clear,]] [[most of the money]] [[is earned]]}} far from the cocoa farms. {{[[Almost two thirds]] goes to}} the retailer and the brand, while taxes and transport {{[[make up]]}} 14 per cent. {{Production, by contrast, [[accounts for]] [[just over a fifth]]}} (16 per cent for processing, 6 per cent for the farmers). {{Taken together, the farmers and the transport companies [[receive a tenth]]}} of the price, 25 cents, which is [[exactly the same amount as]] the state earns in tax.

options.label: List the figures
options.text:
### Analysis of the findings
The retailer and the brand together make out 64 per cent of the price and therefore receive well over the half of the money. Processing accounts for 16 per cent, taxes for 10 per cent and transport for 4 per cent. The cocoa farmers are payed only 6 per cent of the price, or 15 cents per bar.
options.reject: Three typical mistakes: ‘make out’ (→ make up / account for), ‘the half of the money’ (→ half of the money) and ‘payed’ (→ paid).
options.rejectDe: Drei typische Fehler: make out → make up/account for, the half of → half of, payed → paid.
options.textLong:
### Analysis of the findings
The retailer and the brand together make out 64 per cent of the price and therefore receive well over the half of the money. Processing accounts for 16 per cent, taxes for 10 per cent and transport for 4 per cent. The cocoa farmers are payed only 6 per cent of the price, or 15 cents per bar. This means that the retailer earns more than six times as much as the farmers, and the brand over four times as much.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then add the missing figures from the chart and one comparison of your own (… times as much as …, the same amount as …).
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die fehlenden Zahlen aus der Grafik und einen eigenen Vergleich ergänzen (… times as much as …, the same amount as …).

steps.q: Body paragraph 2 (content point 2): how are cocoa farmers and consumers affected?
steps.de: Der zweite Hauptteil erklärt die Folgen für Kakaobäuer:innen und Konsument:innen. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then explain one effect on the farmers and one on consumers in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann je eine Folge für die Bäuer:innen und für Konsument:innen mit eigenen Worten erklären.

options.label: An income to live on
options.text:
### Effects on farmers and consumers
{{The uneven split [[is felt]] most}} at the two ends of the chain. With only 15 cents per bar, many cocoa families earn too little to live on and cannot afford new trees or fertiliser. {{Consumers, on the other hand, seem to benefit from}} low prices, {{but cheap bars make it easy to}} forget the families behind them.
options.why: The topic sentence names both ends of the chain; a chain of cause and effect for farmers, then the consumers’ side.
options.textLong:
### Effects on farmers and consumers
{{The uneven split [[is felt]] most at the two ends of the chain.}} Cocoa farmers, [[as the figures demonstrate,]] gain little from the chocolate their beans [[are turned into]]. {{With only 15 cents per bar, many families}} earn too little to live on. {{As a result, they cannot afford}} new trees or fertiliser, and their harvests shrink. {{Consumers, on the other hand, seem to benefit from}} low prices, which have made chocolate an everyday snack. {{Cheap bars, however, make it easy to}} forget that the cocoa [[was grown]] by families far away who earn very little.

options.label: 15 cents a bar
options.text:
### Effects on farmers and consumers
Low cocoa prices affect more than one group. Most cocoa farms are in West Africa, and the farmers there only get 15 cents for each bar. For instance, consumers buy more and more sweets because they are cheap. The families on the farms work very hard, and the shops make a lot of profit. Some farmers have never even tasted the chocolate that is made from their beans.
options.reject: The paragraph jumps between farmers, consumers and shops, and ‘For instance’ should introduce an example, but cheap sweets for consumers are no example of the farmers’ low pay.
options.rejectDe: Der Absatz springt zwischen Bäuer:innen, Konsument:innen und Geschäften hin und her, und „For instance“ leitet kein passendes Beispiel für den niedrigen Lohn der Bäuer:innen ein.
options.textLong:
### Effects on farmers and consumers
Low cocoa prices affect more than one group. Most cocoa farms are in West Africa, and the farmers there only get 15 cents for each bar. For instance, consumers buy more and more sweets because they are cheap. The families on the farms work very hard, and the shops make a lot of profit. Supermarkets often sell chocolate at special prices, especially before Easter and Christmas. Some farmers have never tasted the chocolate that is made from their beans. Young people in cocoa regions often move to the cities to find other work, and in Europe more and more people buy dark chocolate.

options.label: No future on the farm?
options.text:
### Effects on farmers and consumers
{{A 6 per cent share means hardship for cocoa farmers and a problem for consumers.}} Most cocoa [[is grown]] on small family farms in West Africa, {{where the work pays so badly that}} young people leave for the cities. {{For shoppers, a higher price does not guarantee}} better pay for farmers, as extra money mostly goes to the brand or the shop.
options.why: Names both groups at once, looks ahead for the farmers and explains a less obvious effect on shoppers.
options.textLong:
### Effects on farmers and consumers
{{A 6 per cent share means hardship for cocoa farmers and a problem for consumers.}} Most cocoa [[is grown]] on small family farms in West Africa, {{where the work pays so badly that}} young people leave for the cities. Some regions may soon run out of farmers, which would make cocoa scarcer for everyone. {{For shoppers, the effect is less obvious: a higher price does not guarantee}} better pay for farmers. {{As their share is tiny,}} extra money mostly goes to the brand or the shop, {{and consumers [[therefore]] struggle to}} tell whether a purchase helps at all.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then explain the effects on the farmers and on consumers in your own words, with an example for each.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Folgen für die Bäuer:innen und für Konsument:innen mit eigenen Worten erklären, jeweils mit einem Beispiel.

steps.q: Body paragraph 3 (content point 3): what do we recommend?
steps.de: Der dritte Hauptteil leitet aus den Ergebnissen Empfehlungen für die Schulgemeinschaft ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete the recommendations with your own ideas for the school community.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Empfehlungen mit eigenen Ideen für die Schulgemeinschaft ergänzen.

options.label: Change at the top
options.text:
### Recommendations
It is clear that large chocolate companies decide how the price is shared out, and {EVENT} alone will not change that. These companies must be forced to pay farmers a fair price, and governments should pass laws on minimum prices for cocoa. Shops should also show on every bar how much of the price reaches the farmers.
options.reject: These are demands on companies, governments and shops, not recommendations for the school community. The task asks what the school community can do, so this content point is missed.
options.rejectDe: Forderungen an Konzerne, Politik und Geschäfte statt Empfehlungen für die Schulgemeinschaft: Inhaltspunkt verfehlt.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
It is clear that large chocolate companies decide how the price is shared out, and {EVENT} alone will not change that. These companies must be forced to pay farmers a fair price, and governments should pass laws on minimum prices for cocoa. Shops should also show on every bar how much of the price reaches the farmers, and supermarkets should stop selling chocolate at special prices, as such offers put even more pressure on the farmers. If the retailer’s share fell from 38 to 32 per cent, the farmers’ share could double without any change in the price.

options.label: Raise awareness
options.text:
### Recommendations
{{So that these figures are visible to everyone, it [[is recommended]] that}} the chart [[be displayed]] next to the school shop during {EVENT}, with a short note on what each share pays for. {{In addition, it would be useful to}} invite a speaker from a fair-trade organisation to explain how to recognise trustworthy labels.
options.why: Links back to the figures, then two concrete steps: making the data visible and learning from an expert.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
{{So that these figures are visible to everyone, it [[is recommended]] that}} the chart [[be displayed]] next to the school shop during {EVENT}, with a short note on what each share pays for. {{In addition, it would be useful to}} invite a speaker from a fair-trade organisation to explain how to recognise trustworthy labels. {{The talk could [[be followed]] by}} a class discussion of what fairer pay would cost. {{If the farmers’ 15 cents [[were doubled]],}} the bar would cost €2.65, [[a rise of only 6 per cent]] that most shoppers would barely notice.

options.label: A blind tasting
options.text:
### Recommendations
{{So that consumers can judge for themselves, it [[is recommended]] that}} a blind tasting of fair-trade and ordinary chocolate [[be organised]] as part of {EVENT}. {{Students who find that the fair bars taste just as good}} may be more willing to pay a little extra for them in the school shop.
options.why: Picks up the consumers from the section before and turns the recommendation into a fun event.
options.textLong:
### Recommendations
{{So that consumers can judge for themselves, it [[is recommended]] that}} a blind tasting of fair-trade and ordinary chocolate [[be organised]] as part of {EVENT}. {{Students who find that the fair bars taste just as good}} may be more willing to pay a little extra, {{and [[the figures suggest that]]}} the extra need not be large. If the farmers’ 15 cents [[were doubled]], the bar would cost €2.65, [[a rise of only 6 per cent]]. {{Even if their share [[were tripled]],}} the price would [[increase by just 12 per cent]] to €2.80.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then complete the recommendations with your own ideas and support one of them with figures from the chart.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann die Empfehlungen mit eigenen Ideen ergänzen und eine davon mit Zahlen aus der Grafik begründen.

steps.q: How do we end the report?
steps.de: Der Schluss greift Zweck und Ergebnisse auf und rundet den Report ab. Prüft jede Option: Aufgabe, Aufbau, Wortschatz, Grammatik.
steps.own: Copy the frame. Then complete both sentences in your own words.
steps.ownDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann beide Sätze mit eigenen Worten fertigschreiben.

options.label: Sum up the main finding
options.text:
### Conclusion
{{All in all, [[the figures show]] that}} those who grow the cocoa [[are paid]] very little, a fact that few consumers think about when they buy a cheap bar. {{If the recommendations above [[are followed]],}} the school community can help to change this on a small scale.
options.why: Picks up the findings, both effects and the recommendations without adding anything new.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
{{All in all, [[the figures show]] that}} those who grow the cocoa [[are paid]] very little, {{whereas most of the money goes to}} the companies that sell the chocolate. Few consumers think about this when they buy a cheap bar. {{If the recommendations above [[are followed]],}} the school community can help to change this on a small scale.

options.label: Look ahead to the week
options.text:
### Conclusion
{{To sum up, the chart [[points to]] a clear imbalance}}: those who sell chocolate earn far more than those who grow the cocoa, and few shoppers ever think about it. {{The planned week is}} an ideal chance to make students aware of this.
options.why: Sums up the findings and their effects and ends with the purpose of the report: the planned week of events.
options.textLong:
### Conclusion
{{To sum up, the chart [[points to]] a clear imbalance}}: those who sell chocolate earn far more than those who grow the cocoa, and few shoppers ever think about it. {{The planned week is}} an ideal chance to make students aware of this. {{If the steps recommended above [[are taken]],}} the week could change buying habits at the school for much longer than five days.

steps.ownLong: Copy the frame. Then sum up the findings, the effects and the recommendations in your own words.
steps.ownLongDe: Gerüst abschreiben, dann Ergebnisse, Folgen und Empfehlungen mit eigenen Worten zusammenfassen.

checks.en: Header complete: To, From, Date and a factual subject line
Five sections, each with a clear subheading
The introduction states the purpose and the source of the data
All figures are taken correctly from the chart
All three content points: shares of the price, effects, recommendations
Recommendations for the school community (‘It is recommended that …’)
Formal and impersonal: no contractions, no personal feelings

teacher.aim: Die Klasse baut gemeinsam einen Report (B1+/B2) zu einer erfundenen Preisgrafik und übt dabei, Zahlen präzise zu beschreiben und zu vergleichen, Passivformen gezielt einzusetzen, Folgen zu erklären und Empfehlungen formell zu formulieren.
teacher.prep: A/B/C/D-Karten austeilen (ohne Karten: 1–4 Finger, die Tasten 1–4 wählen wie A–D), Beamer im Vollbild. Die Grafik aus der Aufgabe zusätzlich als Balken- oder Tortendiagramm an die Tafel zeichnen oder ausgedruckt austeilen. Im Gerüst-Modus den eingebauten Timer nutzen: 5 min pro Abschnitt, in der langen Fassung 8–9 min.
teacher.heft: Neue Seite: Datum (rechts), „Report“ als Überschrift. Darunter der Kopf wie am Beamer: To, From, Date, Subject (die Betreffzeile wird im ersten Schritt gewählt). Fünf Abschnitte (Introduction, Analysis of the findings, Effects on farmers and consumers, Recommendations, Conclusion): jeder beginnt nach einer Leerzeile mit seiner Zwischenüberschrift auf einer eigenen Zeile (unterstrichen), darunter der Absatz; am Rand steht nichts. Passivformen und Wendungen für Daten grün unterstreichen.
teacher.flow: 6 Entscheidungen: Betreffzeile und fünf Abschnitte. Volltext kurz (50 min): 5 min Aufgabe und Grafik lesen, 6 Entscheidungen à 2 min, ca. 25 min Abschreiben, 5 min Checkliste. Volltext lang (100 min): dieselben Entscheidungen mit längeren Abschnitten, ca. 45 min Abschreiben, dazu Zeit für die Grafik und die Rechnungen. Gerüst kurz (ca. 60 min): 4 min Aufgabe, pro Abschnitt 1 min Abstimmung, 5–6 min eigenes Schreiben und 1 min Vergleich mit dem Modell; in einer 50-Minuten-Stunde den Schluss als Hausübung und die Checkliste am Beginn der nächsten Stunde. Gerüst lang (100 min): gleicher Ablauf, pro Abschnitt 8–9 min eigenes Schreiben. Die Grafik bleibt die ganze Stunde an der Tafel, weil die Zahlen in den eigenen Sätzen gebraucht werden.
teacher.traps: Introduction C (TA): beginnt sofort mit den Zahlen statt mit Zweck, Auftrag und Datenquelle. Analysis of the findings C (LSA): make out statt make up, the half of statt half of, payed statt paid. Effects on farmers and consumers B (CC): Themensprünge zwischen Bäuer:innen, Konsument:innen und Geschäften, dazu „For instance“ ohne passendes Beispiel. Recommendations A (TA): Forderungen an Konzerne, Politik und Geschäfte statt Empfehlungen für die Schulgemeinschaft. Kürzel: TA = Erfüllung der Aufgabenstellung, CC = Kohärenz und Kohäsion, LSR = Spektrum sprachlicher Mittel, LSA = Sprachrichtigkeit.
teacher.notes: Der Report hat immer fünf Abschnitte (Einleitung, drei Hauptteile, Schluss). Die lange Fassung hat dieselben Entscheidungen mit längeren Abschnitten: Die Einleitung nennt Grenzen der Daten, die Analyse ergänzt einen Vergleich, die Empfehlungen eine Rechnung zu fairen Preisen. Die Zahlen sind für die Aufgabe erfunden (vereinfachtes Beispiel, keine offizielle Statistik). Das Muster ist realistisch: Schätzungen sehen den Anteil der Kakaobäuer:innen am Ladenpreis meist im einstelligen Prozentbereich; der Steueranteil ist gerundet (10 % Umsatzsteuer auf den Nettopreis sind gut 9 % des Endpreises; Schokolade gehört nicht zu den Grundnahrungsmitteln, deren Umsatzsteuer seit 1. Juli 2026 auf 4,9 % gesenkt ist). Das darf die Klasse wissen, es passt gut zur langen Einleitung (Grenzen der Daten). Keine echten Marken nennen oder beschuldigen. Kinderarbeit im Kakaoanbau ist ein reales Thema; falls es aufkommt, sachlich und ohne Einzelschicksale besprechen. Markiert sind Passivformen (auch „It is recommended that …“ und „be displayed“) und Wendungen für Daten, nicht aber Partizipien als Adjektive (a simplified example, the planned week). Für den Namen der Aktionswoche einen englischen Namen rufen lassen, z. B. „Fair Food Week“. Differenzierung: Schnelle ergänzen im Gerüst-Modus einen zusätzlichen Vergleich (… times as much as …) oder formen zwei Aktivsätze ins Passiv um. Hausübung: den Report mit anderen Entscheidungen neu schreiben oder dieselbe Aufgabe mit einer selbst erfundenen Grafik zu einem Kilo Bananen bearbeiten.
